name: LRU Cache (Least Recently Used)
description: High-performance fixed-capacity key-value cache combining an associative hash map with an intrusive doubly linked list to achieve O(1) reads, writes, and evictions.
when_to_use: When memory footprint must be strictly bounded to prevent OOM errors
When recently accessed items are significantly more likely to be accessed again (temporal locality)
Caching expensive database queries, external API responses, or computed tokens
when_not_to_use: When access patterns follow uniform random distribution (eviction overhead without hit improvements)
When frequency of access matters more than recency (use LFU instead)
edge_cases: Capacity equal to 0 or 1
Updating an existing key without modifying list capacity
Re-inserting recently evicted keys
Handling null/undefined values distinctly from non-existent keys

name: Sliding Window Rate Limiter
description: Precision rate limiter tracking granular timestamped request arrivals within a rolling time window using a double-ended queue, avoiding boundary bursts common in fixed-window limiters.

time_complexity.allow: O(k) amortized, where k is expired timestamps pruned

when_to_use: Protecting APIs, recharge endpoints, and payment gateways against burst spikes and brute force
Guaranteeing strict adherence to third-party provider quotas across continuous sliding intervals
Enforcing tenant tier limits without sudden boundary reset surges
when_not_to_use: Extremely memory-constrained environments with millions of keys and high request limits (consider Token Bucket or Leaky Bucket with counter approximations)
When rough 1-minute fixed bucketing is acceptable and memory is primary concern
edge_cases: Requests arriving with non-monotonic timestamps due to system clock drift
Bursts exactly at the limit threshold
Time window boundary rollovers
Empty queues on first check

name: Priority Queue (Min/Max Binary Heap)
description: Array-backed complete binary tree guaranteeing constant-time minimum or maximum element inspection and logarithmic insertion and extraction.
when_to_use: Job queues where urgent background tasks (e.g. VIP recharge, payment webhook) must supersede regular work
Task schedulers sorting tasks by earliest execution timestamp
Top-K streaming elements or graph shortest path algorithms (Dijkstra, Prim)
when_not_to_use: When random access or arbitrary item deletion by value is frequently required (O(N) search)
When strictly strict FIFO ordering without priority is needed (use a Circular Queue or Doubly Linked List)
edge_cases: Extracting from an empty heap
Heap containing elements with equal priority
Custom comparator handling both min-heap and max-heap logic
Dynamic array resizing without memory leaks

name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
description: Tree data structure where each node represents a prefix character, providing deterministic O(M) search, prefix matching, and autocomplete where M is key length.
when_to_use: Autocomplete and predictive search in product catalogs, user lookup, or recharge billers
API route matching and URL path prefix resolution
IP routing (longest prefix match) and phone directory area code resolution
when_not_to_use: When keys do not share common prefixes, leading to sparse trees with high memory overhead
When exact-match-only is needed and hash maps provide simpler O(1) performance
edge_cases: Inserting empty string
Searching for prefix that is not a complete terminal word
Deleting a word whose prefix belongs to another longer word
Unicode and multi-byte character support

name: Bloom Filter
description: Space-efficient probabilistic bit array utilizing multiple independent hash functions to test set membership with zero false negatives and tunable false positive probability.

time_complexity.add: O(k), where k is number of hash functions

when_to_use: Preventing duplicate transaction and recharge processing prior to touching expensive databases
Negative cache lookup to protect databases from queries on non-existent keys (preventing cache penetration)
Deduplicating billions of crawled URLs or logs in limited memory
when_not_to_use: When false positives cannot be tolerated under any circumstances
When items must be deleted dynamically (standard Bloom filter doesn't support deletion; use Counting Bloom Filter instead)
edge_cases: Bit saturation when element count exceeds expected capacity, causing false positive rate to spike
Hash collisions between distinct items
Sizing bit array and hash count based on mathematical error rate formulas

name: Consistent Hash Ring
description: Distributed hashing scheme mapping keys and servers to a 360-degree hash ring using virtual nodes, ensuring minimal key relocation when nodes are added or removed.

time_complexity.addNode: O(v * log(N * v)) where v is virtual nodes and N is server count
time_complexity.getNode: O(log(N * v)) via binary search on ring

when_to_use: Distributing cache keys or user sessions across a dynamic cluster of Redis/Memcached servers
Microservice sharding and load balancing with sticky session affinity
Minimizing cache eviction cascades during cluster scaling events
when_not_to_use: Single-node or static deployments where simple modulo hashing (`hash(key) % N`) is sufficient
Systems with strict leader-follower replication requiring consensus (e.g. Raft)
edge_cases: Zero nodes registered in the ring
Uneven hash distribution mitigated by configuring virtual replica counts
Removing a non-existent node
Wrap-around ring boundaries when key hash exceeds maximum server hash

name: Monotonic Deque (Sliding Window Extremes)
description: Double-ended monotonic queue maintaining elements in strictly decreasing or increasing order to compute sliding window minimums, maximums, and statistics in O(1) amortized time.
space_complexity: O(w) where w is window size
when_to_use: Calculating continuous 5-minute peak transaction latency or maximum recharge amount in a streaming pipeline
Real-time fraud spike detection over sliding transaction windows
Algorithmic trading metrics (moving Bollinger bands, sliding maximum drawdowns)
when_not_to_use: When the window size is dynamic and requires random element removals by ID
When cumulative sums or averages are required (use Prefix Sums instead)
edge_cases: Stream window smaller than window size
Duplicate values equal to current extremum
Monotonically strictly decreasing or strictly increasing streams

name: Disjoint Set Union (Union-Find)
description: High-efficiency partition tracking structure with path compression and union-by-rank, providing near-constant time O(alpha(n)) equivalence queries and set mergers.
when_to_use: Detecting circular transaction networks and fraud rings where money loops across suspicious accounts
Dynamic network connectivity tracking and cluster partition analysis
Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree algorithm for cost-optimized server wiring
when_not_to_use: When edge weights or shortest paths are needed (use Dijkstra or Bellman-Ford)
When sets must be dynamically split or isolated elements removed (classical Disjoint Set does not support easy separation)
edge_cases: Querying non-existent nodes
Connecting an element to itself (noop)
Deep uncompressed trees without union-by-rank fallback
Cycle detection when an edge connects two elements already in the same root

name: Doubly Linked List
description: Bidirectional sequential data structure supporting O(1) prepend, append, and node removal given a node reference, serving as the foundational backbone for LRU caches and queues.
when_to_use: Building composite structures like LRU Caches or LFU Caches requiring constant-time arbitrary node detachment and re-attachment
Deque implementations requiring fast insertions and deletions at both ends without array copy overhead
when_not_to_use: When random indexed access (`get(index)`) is frequent (O(N) traversal vs O(1) array access)
When memory footprint per element is critical (pointers incur 2x-3x memory overhead)
edge_cases: Operations on empty list
Removing head or tail node
List containing only one single element
Dangling pointers during detachment

name: Binary Search & Bound Locator
description: Logarithmic search algorithm over sorted sequences providing exact match lookup, lower bound (first index >= target), and upper bound (first index > target) queries.
when_to_use: Looking up transaction logs within timestamp ranges in indexed in-memory tables
Finding applicable discount tier, tax bracket, or billing fee based on numerical recharge thresholds
Fast sorted catalog filtering
when_not_to_use: Unsorted data where the cost of sorting (O(n log n)) exceeds linear scan (O(n))
Linked lists without direct random access (binary search degrades to O(n))
edge_cases: Integer overflow during midpoint calculation `(low + high) / 2`
Target smaller than first element or larger than last element
Arrays with duplicate matching elements
Empty arrays

name: Prefix Sum & Range Query Engine
description: Preprocessing technique storing running cumulative totals to answer range sum queries over arbitrary intervals in strictly O(1) time.
when_to_use: Instantaneous calculation of user recharge totals or revenue between two dates
Aggregating request counts and error telemetry over arbitrary time slices without looping
Financial ledger auditing and balance reconciliation across transaction indices
when_not_to_use: Frequently mutated arrays where each update requires recomputing prefix sums in O(n) time (use a Fenwick Tree / Binary Indexed Tree or Segment Tree instead)
edge_cases: Out of bounds index requests
Query where start index is 0
Single element range query
64-bit integer overflow during massive financial accumulations

name: Retry Queue with Exponential Backoff & Full Jitter
description: Resilient retry orchestration mechanism utilizing a min-heap priority queue and exponential backoff with full jitter to prevent thundering herd problems during upstream outages.

time_complexity.pollReady: O(log n) when items ready, O(1) peek when not

when_to_use: Retrying transiently failed payment webhooks, telecom recharge dispatches, and third-party bank API calls
Preventing server self-inflicted DDoS after recovering from a service outage (decorrelated jitter)
Dead-letter queue (DLQ) routing after exhausting maximum retry thresholds
when_not_to_use: Non-idempotent operations where re-executing could cause duplicate state side-effects without deduplication
Permanent client errors (e.g. 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized) that will never succeed on retry
edge_cases: Exponential backoff calculation exceeding maximum backoff cap (capping required)
Clock shifts or negative retry delays
Reaching max retry attempts and routing to dead letter handler
Concurrent or out-of-order execution readiness
